newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klima hails French left victory.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klima hails French left victory.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima on Monday greeted the election victory of the Socialists and their allies in France, but the far right said the result showed growing opposition in the European Union to a single currency.

"I am convinced that France with its new government will continue to be an engine with regard to European integration...and will help to give a stronger social dimension to the European Union," Austrian Social Democrat leader Klima said in a statement.
Far-right leader Joerg Haider said the French result highlighted voters' concerns about the single currency and predicted that euro supporters would lose across Europe.

"The French elections are also a clear warning that the Austrian government should not decide on the euro issue over the heads of the population and endanger the schilling unnecessarily," Haider said.
Haider's Freedom Party scored an all-time high with 28 percent of the vote in European parliament elections last year, making it the strongest far right grouping in Europe.
Austria's political and financial leaders are staunch backers of European economic and monetary union (EMU) and have pledged to be among the first EU nations to join the single currency in 1999.
